name: Citizenship by Descent

qualifying_event.description: A child born outside Trinidad and Tobago to a parent who is a citizen of Trinidad and Tobago otherwise than by descent is entitled to a certificate of citizenship by descent.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificate; parent's proof of T&T citizenship (not itself acquired by descent).

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a parent who is a citizen of Trinidad and Tobago otherwise than by descent (i.e. by birth in the territory, naturalisation, or registration) -- children of a parent who is themselves a citizen BY DESCENT do not qualify under this provision.
Application must be made by the responsible parent/guardian before the child turns 18, or by the child within 1 year of attaining the age of majority.

evidence_required.document: Parent's proof of T&T citizenship (not by descent)
Applicant Information for Passport Applications (citizens by descent) documentation

sources.title: Citizenship of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago Act, Chapter 1:50 (primary legislation, privately hosted mirror): citizenship by descent for a child born abroad to a citizen-otherwise-than-by-descent parent, application timing rules, one-generation-only limit
Ministry of Foreign and CARICOM Affairs, Government of Trinidad and Tobago -- Applicant Information for Passport Applications for Citizens of Trinidad and Tobago by Descent

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Trinidad and Tobago's initial build. IMPORTANT, easy-to-miss rule confirmed directly in the primary Act text: citizenship by descent does NOT chain across multiple generations born abroad -- a child of a parent who is themselves a citizen by descent does NOT qualify under this provision, meaning descent-based citizenship effectively skips at most one generation born outside the territory. This is a materially different (stricter) descent rule than most non-BOT sovereign countries built earlier this session, where descent citizenship is typically modelled without an explicit one-generation cutoff -- flagged prominently since it changes the practical answer for grandchildren of citizens born abroad.
